column1: # Two cross-leg rules on the Luau table runtime (review 2026-11-21), read by
# TestLuauCompressedFloatF32Range. A compressed float's declared range is
# compared at float32 (docs/SPEC.md §4.6: every runtime evaluates the triple
# at float32), so 0.1f under max = 0.1 is written and read in every form, a
# double that rounds to 0.1f is held as 0.1f, and a value past the float32 end
# is still refused. A compressed float holding -0 is +0 (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md
# form, and what the probe does with input:
#   var              save the number in V, read it back strictly
#   var-save-same    save the two numbers; as_plus when the bytes are equal
#   json             read the JSON text as V
#   json-write-sign  write the number as JSON; minus when the text holds -0
#   json-roundtrip   write the number as JSON and read that text back
#   json-write       write the number as JSON
#   text             read the text form as V
#   fixed            save the number as a fixed F row, load it back
#   message          save the number in an F message, load it back
# above 0.1f that rounds to it; -0 is negative zero.
# want: read:<value at %.9g>, read, refused, refused:<reason>, as_plus, plus,
#       written. A refusal is compared by verdict and, where this Luau test
#       pinned it, by the reason the Luau runtime names.
# the JSON read and write, and the text form
